assumptions.assumption: The 1,000+ SF vehicles were bought by riders who work the SF 'core delivery zone' (SoMa+Mission+Tenderloin+FiDi), so 'SF core zone vs DTLA+Koreatown (180-200k residents)' is a like-for-like scaling base.
assumptions.why_it_may_be_wrong: 415 eBikes at 6th & Folsom is within a 15-minute e-bike ride of essentially all of SF's 7x7, and many couriers live in Daly City, the Excelsior/Bayview, Oakland and beyond and commute in. The installed base is almost certainly a whole-city (and partly Bay Area) count, not a core-zone count. If only 30-50% of buyers primarily work SoMa/Mission/TL/FiDi, then dividing 1,000 vehicles by the core-zone population and multiplying by DTLA+Koreatown overstates LA potential by 2-3x. Worse, LA's two target zones (DTLA and Koreatown) are ~5 miles apart with a single hub on the far east edge of one of them, so the LA 'core' is not one contiguous catchment the way SoMa-to-Mission is.
assumptions.magnitude: 2-3x overstatement of the LA rider pool if SF customers are city-wide; the Koreatown half of the LA zone may behave as a separate, unserved market.
assumptions.cheap_test: Pull home ZIP / billing ZIP for every SF buyer and renter from Shopify and Stripe and the rental contracts; bucket by ZIP (94103/94110/94102/94105/94107 vs everything else, vs non-SF). Separately, stand at 5 SF delivery hotspots outside the core (Richmond/Clement, Sunset/Irving, Bayview/3rd St, Chinatown, Marina) at Friday 6-9pm and count HMP-style mopeds vs the same count at 5 core hotspots.
assumptions.hmp_internal_data_needed: Customer address ZIP for all sales and rental contracts since 2022; service-ticket ZIPs; pickup-service (broken vehicle) addresses; battery-rental customer addresses.

assumptions.assumption: LA can reach meaningful scale (hundreds of active riders, 100 rentals, 300 battery subscribers) by M12-M24 because the SF playbook is proven; the SF curve is treated as a template for LA year 1-2.
assumptions.why_it_may_be_wrong: Public reporting (Gazetteer SF) says HMP launched in 2022 and has 600+ e-mopeds operating in SF with a target of 1,000 by end-2026, i.e. ~4 years to the current base, in a market where HMP had the SF delivery-moped niche largely to itself and captured roughly 30% of the ~2,000 active Uber Eats/DoorDash couriers cited for SF. That growth compounded through a closed rider community (word-of-mouth cited by every rider interviewed). LA year 1 resembles SF year 1 (2022-23), not SF year 4: no reputation, no referral base, competitors (Zoomo Leimert Park, Whizz LA at $139/mo) already present. The M3/M6/M12 triggers will be set off the mature SF numbers and will look like failure even if LA is tracking SF's own year-1 pace. Note also the discrepancy between '600+ operating' (press) and '>1,000 sold' (founder): both could be true only if ~40% of sold units are no longer active.
assumptions.magnitude: If SF sold 150-300 units in its first 12 months, LA year-1 sales of 100-250 units are the realistic base case; at ~$10k/mo rent plus 2-3 staff and a replacement fleet, M12 cash break-even is unlikely and the lease burns $120k+ before the trigger math is even meaningful.
assumptions.cheap_test: Export monthly unit sales and new rental starts from Shopify/Stripe since day one, plot cumulative units by month-since-launch, and set LA triggers off that curve (SF M3/M6/M12/M24 actuals), not off 2026 totals. Cross-check: count Google/Yelp reviews by year for 415 eBikes as a rough growth-shape proxy (shape only, not level, given the known review-count error).
assumptions.hmp_internal_data_needed: Monthly units sold, rentals started, battery rentals started, 2022-2026; marketing spend by month; share of first-year sales that were referrals.

assumptions.assumption: Riders in DTLA/Koreatown will adopt at SF-like rates and SF-like CAC (near-zero, word-of-mouth) once a hub exists.
assumptions.why_it_may_be_wrong: SF adoption rides on a specific, dense immigrant courier community: riders quoted in press are Nepali (Oli, Basnet), there is a 500-member Bay Area WeChat group of Chinese-speaking delivery/rideshare drivers, the founder's prior venture (Xiaocun) targeted the Chinese-speaking community, and the core value prop is 'class 2, no license/registration/insurance' for riders without California driver's licenses. That network does not exist in LA on day one. DTLA/Westlake/Pico-Union couriers are predominantly Latino/Spanish-speaking and Koreatown adds a Korean-speaking layer; their channels are WhatsApp/Facebook/TikTok, not WeChat, and there is no HMP-riding cousin to vouch for the product. 2025-26 immigration enforcement in exactly these LA neighborhoods (DTLA, Fashion District, MacArthur Park) makes unlicensed riders less willing to sign KYC-heavy rental contracts or be visibly mobile, and makes 'no license needed' both more valuable and more legally exposed.
assumptions.magnitude: CAC could move from roughly $0-50 (referral) in SF to $150-400 per rider (paid social, street promoters, bilingual staff) in LA; rental-to-purchase conversion could be half SF's rate for the first 12-18 months.
assumptions.cheap_test: Before signing: 3 dinner-shift field counts (Fri/Sat/Sun 6-9pm) outside 10 high-volume Koreatown BBQ/DTLA restaurants and the CloudKitchens/ghost-kitchen sites; log vehicle type, and ask 30+ riders their language, where they got their vehicle, and which group chat they use. Join LA courier Facebook/WhatsApp/Telegram groups and post a rental offer to measure inbound interest. Check Zoomo LA (Leimert Park) and Whizz LA review volume and rider nationality mix as a proxy.
assumptions.hmp_internal_data_needed: Preferred language / country of origin of SF customers (from sales records, WeChat vs WhatsApp contact), share of sales tagged as referrals, license status distribution of buyers, any LA-area inbound inquiries already received.

assumptions.assumption: DTLA/Koreatown parking pain pushes LA couriers onto two-wheelers the way SF's density does, so the addressable pool is 'all app couriers in the zone' and higher-speed mopeds/e-motorcycles simply extend the SF product ladder.
assumptions.why_it_may_be_wrong: LA app couriers are overwhelmingly car-based; two-wheeler share is growing (DoorDash reports 2-wheeler deliveries growing ~4x faster than car, 2024-25) but from a low base, whereas in SF's core the two-wheeler is already the default and HMP mopeds are the recognizable delivery vehicle. A car-first rider who switches in LA needs range and 35-50 mph to be competitive over longer LA trip legs, which pushes the product toward Lightning MK.II / e-motorcycle class vehicles that require a license, registration, insurance and an M1/M2 endorsement, destroying the 'no license' value prop that drove SF sales and raising the ticket size for a lower-earning rider. The SF installed base is dominated by 20 mph class-2-styled mopeds; there is little SF evidence that HMP can sell or rent licensed 40-70 mph vehicles at volume.
assumptions.magnitude: Addressable two-wheel couriers in DTLA+Koreatown may be 300-800 active riders, not several thousand; at an SF-like 30% share ceiling that is 100-250 vehicles, and the licensed-vehicle share of that has a different (lower) conversion and higher warranty/insurance friction.
assumptions.cheap_test: Field mode-split count (car / e-bike / moped / e-motorcycle / scooter) at 10 LA hotspots vs 10 SF hotspots at the same hour; check whether Uber/DoorDash 'bike/scooter' onboarding in LA is waitlisted (a demand signal); look at Whizz LA and Zoomo LA pricing and fleet type (they run 20-28 mph e-bikes, implying that is where LA two-wheel demand sits).
assumptions.hmp_internal_data_needed: SF sales mix by model and speed class (FLASH vs Lightning vs SWFT vs e-bike) 2022-2026; share of Lightning MK.II buyers who are delivery riders vs enthusiasts; return/complaint rate on licensed vehicles; average daily miles per rider from battery/GPS data.

assumptions.assumption: 'Sell the vehicle, keep renting the battery' (300+ of 1,000+ buyers in SF) and whole-vehicle rental will transfer to a single hub at 768 Ceres, so battery subscriptions become LA's recurring revenue engine.
assumptions.why_it_may_be_wrong: In SF the shop sits inside the delivery zone, so a battery swap, warranty swap, or rental return is a 5-10 minute detour. 768 Ceres is ~1.7 mi from the DTLA core, ~3.5 mi from USC and ~5 mi from Wilshire/Western in Koreatown, which is 25-35 minutes each way on a 20 mph e-bike in traffic, on the edge of Skid Row, at night. A Koreatown rider will not lose an hour of dinner-peak earnings to swap or service a battery. Riders in LA also live far from where they work (South LA, Pico-Union, SGV), so home charging beats hub swapping. Battery attach rate is a function of distance to shop, and the LA distance distribution is much worse. Additionally, SF's swap stations only launched June 2026, so the 300+ SF battery renters are mostly home-charging rentals; there is no SF evidence yet that swap-hub economics work anywhere.
assumptions.magnitude: Battery subscription attach could fall from ~30% of buyers to 5-15% for riders outside a 1.5-mile radius of Ceres; recurring battery revenue could be one-third of an SF-scaled projection, and rental-vehicle utilization drops as pickup/return friction rises.
assumptions.cheap_test: Compute SF battery-rental attach rate and churn by customer distance from 6th & Folsom (0-1 mi / 1-2 / 2-4 / 4+), then apply LA target-zone distances to 768 Ceres. Ride from Wilshire/Western to 768 Ceres at 6:30pm on a FLASH and time it. Ask 30 Koreatown riders whether they would ride to 7th & Ceres for a battery.
assumptions.hmp_internal_data_needed: Battery-rental customer addresses, swap/exchange frequency per subscriber, subscriber churn by distance, share of SF battery renters who use the June-2026 swap station vs home charging, rental-return and service-visit frequency.

assumptions.assumption: The SF installed base is a stable, repeatable outcome of the model rather than an artifact of a particular 2022-2025 period.
assumptions.why_it_may_be_wrong: HMP's SF sales accumulated 2022-2026 alongside (a) an unusual inflow of newly arrived migrants (press cites Nepal, Venezuela, Morocco) who needed license-free income immediately, (b) SF's exceptionally high per-capita app-delivery demand (downtown malls reported to be kept alive by food delivery; low car ownership; high incomes), and (c) tolerant local enforcement of 3-5 kW 'class 2' mopeds. All three are shifting: 2025-26 immigration enforcement reduces the inflow and raises rider risk; per-order pay on the apps has fallen; SF is now debating moped-styled e-bike enforcement. If SF's own new-customer rate has already slowed in 2025-26, an LA hub sized from 2023-24 SF cohorts is sized to a market that no longer exists even in SF.
assumptions.magnitude: If SF new-customer acquisition in the last 12 months is 30-50% below its 2023-24 peak, LA projections built on lifetime SF averages are overstated by the same amount; the LA lease would be a bet on re-creating peak-SF conditions in a harder city.
assumptions.cheap_test: Plot SF new buyers and new renters per month for the last 36 months; check whether 2025-26 quarters are flat or declining versus 2023-24. Cross-check with SF Environment Department / MissionLocal courier counts by year and with Uber/DoorDash LA onboarding waitlists.
assumptions.hmp_internal_data_needed: New-customer counts by month and cohort (2022-2026), renter-to-buyer conversion by cohort, rental churn by cohort, country-of-origin mix by cohort if recorded.

assumptions.assumption: '>1,000 sold' is the right base for scaling LA revenue per rider (parts, service, batteries, upgrades).
assumptions.why_it_may_be_wrong: Public reporting puts HMP at '600+ e-mopeds operating in SF' with a target of 1,000 by end-2026, while the founder counts '>1,000 sold'. Both can be true only if roughly 40% of sold units are no longer active (theft, write-offs, riders who quit or left the region, vehicles resold). The active revenue-generating base is therefore ~600, not ~1,000, and 100 rentals + 300 battery renters should be expressed as shares of active riders (~17% and ~50%), not of cumulative sales. Scaling LA from cumulative sales inflates recurring revenue per 'customer' by ~40%; LA's theft environment (Skid Row edge) will make the LA active/sold ratio worse than SF's.
assumptions.magnitude: 30-50% overstatement of the active base and of recurring revenue per vehicle sold; this changes the M12/M24 trigger definitions (active riders, battery subscribers) rather than the go decision by itself.
assumptions.cheap_test: Count distinct SF vehicles (by VIN/frame number or customer) with any service visit, part purchase, battery exchange or rental payment in the last 90 days, and divide by cumulative units sold; compare with the '600+' press figure. Reconcile any Google-review-based estimate against this (the known past error).
assumptions.hmp_internal_data_needed: Last-service-date and last-purchase-date per VIN/customer, active battery-rental accounts, GPS/app-active units if any, theft and total-loss reports by year.
